S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.

subtypes.With Depressed Mood: Symptoms mainly include low mood, tearfulness, or feelings of hopelessness.
subtypes.With Anxiety: Symptoms mainly include nervousness, worry, jitteriness, or separation anxiety.
subtypes.With Mixed Anxiety and Depressed Mood: A combination of depression and anxiety symptoms appears.
subtypes.With Disturbance of Conduct: Symptoms mainly involve violation of rules, truancy, vandalism, reckless driving, or fighting.
subtypes.With Mixed Disturbance of Emotions and C: Both emotional symptoms (depression, anxiety) and behavioral problems appear together.
subtypes.Unspecified: Maladaptive reactions not classified into the above types (e.g., physical complaints, social withdrawal).

patient_info.stressor_event: Gaining a new family member (e.g., birth, adoption, older adult moving in)
patient_info.stressor: John’s stressor started when his elderly father-in-law moved into the Tiemann household after a decline in independence, turning their quiet South Texas home into a shared caregiving space just as John was balancing EMT shifts and paramedic coursework. He initially approached the change with the same practical service ethic he brought to EMS, rearranging the garage, garden schedule, and family routines without complaint. Over 4 months, the ongoing household demands produced a maladaptive stress response that began to affect his concentration during administrative tasks, his attendance at community first-aid workshops, and the fishing and woodworking routines that usually kept him steady. He recognized the pattern himself during a continuing-education seminar on responder wellness and asked his primary care doctor for a referral to a psychiatrist.

S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.
S081.manifestation: I came in because ever since my father-in-law moved in with us, I’ve been holding it together at work, but at home and with my coursework I’m more wound up and short than I’m used to, and I’ve started skipping the fishing, woodworking, and first-aid workshops that usually keep my head clear.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.description: Symptoms must develop within 3 months of the onset of the stressor
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: My father-in-law moved in about four months ago, and I started noticing the strain within the first couple of months as our home routines and caregiving demands settled in.

additional_requirement_2.name: Additional Requirement 2
additional_requirement_2.description: Within 6 months of the termination of the stressor or its consequences
additional_requirement_2.manifestation: There hasn’t really been a stopping point yet because my father-in-law is still living with us and we’re still adjusting to the caregiving setup.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: I’m still doing my EMT work, but I’ve fallen behind on some paramedic coursework and stopped showing up consistently for the community first-aid workshops I usually help with.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on for about four months, since my father-in-law moved into our house.
